title: Deployment choice criteria — retail POC
content:
Background:
This doc captures our internal decision criteria and recommended deployment approach for the Retail Co. conversational product POC. Retail Co wants a storefront virtual assistant that can: handle product lookups, personalized suggestions, returns flow, and tiered escalation to humans. They care about user experience (sub-200ms token latency at p95 for short queries), cost predictability during peak holiday traffic, and strict customer-data controls for payment-related flows (PCI scope).

Goals for the POC (what success looks like):
- Functional: demo end-to-end flows (search, upsell, returns) to business stakeholders within 4 weeks.
- Performance: p95 generation latency < 350ms for 32-token replies during peak; p50 < 150ms.
- Cost: predictable monthly bill within the customer’s POC budget (~$12k/month) or clear committed-price path for Dedicated.
- Security/compliance: payment flows must not leave customer-controlled infrastructure; audit logs and KMS required.
- Ops: automated tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and a rollback path to simpler models.

Constraints and assumptions (explicit):
- Traffic pattern: baseline 5 QPS, expected holiday spike to 120 QPS for short bursts (~2–4 hours/day across peak week). Burstiness matters more than sustained throughput.
- Typical prompt length: 80–200 tokens; responses usually 16–64 tokens.
- Sensitive paths: checkout/returns contain PII/payment tokens; these must be routed to an environment where data residency and KMS control are customer-managed.
- Allowed timeframe: POC must be deployable in ~2 weeks for hosted-only and ~4–6 weeks for Dedicated/private with infra support.
- Model choices: using an open LLM baseline we onboarded (retail-13b-opt) with a quantized 4-bit variant available for Dedicated/Private.

Hard non-functional requirements from the customer:
- PCI-scope: all payment authorization prompts must be handled within Private or customer-managed VPC.
- Audit logs retention for PII flows: 90 days with read-only export to customer SIEM.
- Uptime: POC demo requires <2% errors during reserved demo windows.

Option summaries and tradeoffs:
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted)
  Pros:
  - Fastest to set up: full pipeline (API, telemetry, UI hooks) in days.
  - Managed autoscaling handles burst spikes with minimal ops.
  - Low friction for model updates and function calls.
  - Observability: token-level cost and latency dashboards out of the box.
  Cons:
  - Data residency/KMS controls limited: cannot meet PCI requirement for payment flows unless we build synthetic routing (split flow) which increases complexity.
  - Cost variability during holiday spikes; usage-based pricing may exceed POC budget without dedicated discount.
  - Less deterministic tail latency at massive bursts compared to reserved capacity.
  Rough estimates (POC monthly): baseline $3–6k; peak-heavy month $8–20k depending on token volumes and streaming usage.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity in Redwood Dedicated)
  Pros:
  - Predictable throughput and tail latency for reserved GPU pools; better for bursty retail traffic.
  - Can provision quantized model variants and pinned model versions for repeatable performance.
  - Option to restrict data flow and limited private connectivity; better SLAs and enterprise support.
  - Cost predictability with a committed monthly fee; may fit POC budget if committed for short term.
  Cons:
  - Longer lead time to provision (2–4 weeks depending on capacity).
  - Requires engineering time to tune autoscaling and batching profiles.
  - Still may not satisfy full PCI data residency unless paired with Private deployment for sensitive subset.
  Rough estimates (POC monthly committed): $15–35k for a small reserved pool capable of 120QPS burst (depends on GPU type and packing).

3) Private (customer VPC or on-prem)
  Pros:
  - Full control over data residency, KMS/HSM, and network. Meets hard PCI requirement when set up correctly.
  - Deterministic performance if customer-provided hardware is sized properly.
  - Enables additional security controls (air-gapped dev lanes, SIEM ingest).
  Cons:
  - Longest setup time and highest operational lift for the POC (infra procurement, networking, config).
  - Higher upfront cost and customer needs infra/ops competency.
  - Less flexible for rapid model iteration unless we provide direct service/support.
  Rough estimates (POC monthly run rate if using customer infra): infra amortization + ops support ~$8–25k (customer-dependent) plus Redwood private license fees.

Sizing notes and quick capacity sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Target peak: 120 QPS with 32-token outputs. With batching and quantized model we can expect ~22 tokens/s inference per A100-equivalent GPU for small model variant or higher for newer GPUs.
- Conservative Dedicated pool: 4–6 A100-equivalent GPUs with multi-tenant packing and dynamic batching to sustain bursty peak with warm KV caches.
- Private sizing: mirror Dedicated numbers; but customer may opt for fewer higher-performance GPUs depending on cost.

Routing & hybrid pattern recommended for this POC (practical compromise):
- Non-sensitive conversational traffic -> Hosted API (fastest, low friction).
- Payment/returns flows (sensitive) -> Private (customer VPC) or Dedicated with explicit network peering + KMS escrow depending on customer's security posture.
- Fallback behavior: if Private/Dedicated capacity constrained, route to hosted but with redaction/proxy layer that strips PII and returns a safe fallback message (requires product acceptance).

Model & perf tactics to control cost and latency:
- Use quantized model for Dedicated/Private to shrink GPU footprint.
- Aggressive prefix KV caching for FAQ/product-description content.
- Adaptive batching windows: low-latency route for interactive users (smaller batches but guaranteed SLO), batch route for background tasks.
- Response length caps for chat path with “more info” expansion to limit token costs.

Monitoring, SLOs, and alerting (must-haves for POC):
- Dashboards: p50/p95/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, tail error rate by route, KV cache hit ratio, queue lengths.
- Alerts: p95 latency > 400ms for 10m, token cost > expected burn rate, dropped requests > 0.5% during demo windows.
- Audit logs: separate retention policy for PII/payment routes with immediate export to customer SIEM.

Recommendation (short):
- Adopt a hybrid routing approach for the POC: deploy core non-sensitive flows to Redwood Hosted (fast onboarding) and provision a small Private tenant (or Dedicated with strict peering) to handle payment/returns flows only. This balances demo velocity, budget control, and meeting the hard PCI requirement.
- Tactic: Launch hosted-only internal demo in 1 week to validate dialog flows and instrumentation, then stand up Dedicated/Private for sensitive routing in parallel (2–4 weeks).

Decision criteria checklist (scorecard for final choice):
- Meets PCI requirement for sensitive flows? (Yes/No)
- Onboarding time <= 2 weeks for initial demo?
- P95 latency under target at peak?
- POC monthly cost within $12k budget or visible committed discount?
- Ops burden acceptable to customer (SRE/infra support)?

Open questions / blockers:
- Customer infra readiness for Private: do they have available GPUs or a cloud VPC budget? (action: sales to confirm by EOD Fri).
- Legal: can we accept redaction-based fallback for payment flows temporarily during the demo? (action: legal consult, ticket RET-1892).
- Exact token volume estimate for holiday spike — we used QPS proxy; ask customer for expected session counts.

Next steps (owners & timeline):
- This week: run hosted proof-of-concept flow keyed to demo scenarios (owner: Priya, due: +5 business days).
- Parallel: Solutions Eng to create Dedicated capacity request and cost quote (owner: Miguel, due: +7 business days).
- Security: Liaise with customer security on KMS/HSM options and create Private deployment checklist (owner: Lena, due: +10 business days).
- Create a short playbook for split-routing and redaction fallback for demo scripts (owner: Conor, due: +4 business days).

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep model changes small during demo windows. Avoid retraining or heavy fine-tuning; use prompt engineering and tool-calling for stateful flows.
- If customer is sensitive to cost, show them Dedicated committed pricing vs hosted forecast with burn charts — that often unlocks committed spend.
- Track audit log export path early; customers get nervous if we leave that to the last minute.

Attachments referenced: design sketch in RET-POC-Overview Confluence, jira RET-1892 (legal), GH PR for demo app.
